title: The Quality Practice

header.html: Explain the purpose of the quality practice and its relationships with the principles; explain the purpose of the product description, quality management approach, quality register and product register; define user quality expectations, acceptance criteria, quality specifications and requirements; describe quality planning, quality control and quality assurance
the official PRINCE2 7 Foundation syllabus (PeopleCert), learning outcome 4.4

html:
1Purpose

The quality practice defines and implements the means by which the project will create products that are fit for purpose: products that meet user needs and can be accepted. It supports focus on products.

2Key concepts

Term Meaning
User quality expectations What the users expect of the product's quality
Acceptance criteria The measurable conditions a product must meet to be accepted
Quality specifications The detailed measures (standards, tolerances) the product must meet
Requirements What the product must do or provide (needs, features)
Exam tip

. Expectations come from users; acceptance criteria say how acceptance is judged; specifications give the detailed measures. All are agreed before work starts.

3Quality planning, control and assurance

Activity Meaning Who
Quality planning Decide how quality will be achieved: standards, criteria, methods, responsibilities Project manager with the team and assurance input
Quality control Check products against their criteria (tests, reviews, inspections) and record results The team producing and checking the work
Quality assurance Independent assessment that the quality processes are working and the project is on track to meet needs Project assurance or an independent function
Exam tip

. Control checks the product. Assurance checks the system and the process. If the checker is independent of the team, think assurance.

4Management products

Product Purpose
Product description Describes a product's purpose, composition, derivation, format and quality criteria, plus how quality will be checked
Quality management approach (PID) How quality will be achieved on the project
Quality register (project log) A record of all quality checks planned and done, and their results
Product register (project log) A record of the products, their status and approval
Exam tip

. Acceptance criteria, user quality expectations and quality specifications are agreed before the product is built, not after.

5Exam Q&A

5.1 Practice questions (choose the best answer)

S1A tester runs a set of checks on a delivered component and records the results. Which activity is this?

  • AQuality planning
  • BQuality assurance
  • CRisk analysis
  • DQuality control
Show the answer

Answer: D. Checking products against criteria is quality control.

S2Which statements are CORRECT? (1) Quality control checks products against their criteria. (2) Quality assurance independently assesses whether quality processes work. (3) Quality planning happens only after delivery. (4) Quality assurance is carried out by the team that builds the product.

  • A3 and 4
  • B2 and 3
  • C1 and 2
  • D1 and 4
Show the answer

Answer: C. Control checks products; assurance independently assesses the quality system.

S3Identify the missing word. [ ? ] are the measurable conditions a product must meet to be accepted.

  • ATolerances
  • BDependencies
  • CStages
  • DAcceptance criteria
Show the answer

Answer: D. That is the definition of acceptance criteria.

S4Which register records every planned and completed quality check with its results?

  • AProduct register
  • BRisk register
  • CQuality register
  • DIssue register
Show the answer

Answer: C. The quality register records quality checks and results.

S5Which document describes a product's purpose, composition and quality criteria?

  • AHighlight report
  • BEnd project report
  • CProduct description
  • DLessons report
Show the answer

Answer: C. That is a product description.

S6Which principle does the quality practice most directly support?

  • AFocus on products
  • BManage by stages
  • CLearn from experience
  • DDefine roles
Show the answer

Answer: A. Quality starts from defining products and their criteria.

5.2 Recall questions

R1What is the purpose of the quality practice?

Show the answer

To create products that are fit for purpose.

R2Define acceptance criteria.

Show the answer

The measurable conditions a product must meet to be accepted.

R3Which activity checks products against their criteria?

Show the answer

Quality control.

R4Which activity is an independent assessment of the quality processes?

Show the answer

Quality assurance.

R5What does the product register record?

Show the answer

The products, their status and approval.

R6Where is the quality approach recorded?

Show the answer

In the quality management approach, part of the PID.

6Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
Purpose create products that are fit for purpose
Concepts user quality expectations, acceptance criteria, quality specifications, requirements
Activities planning (decide), control (check product), assurance (independent check of the system)
Products product description, quality management approach, quality register, product register
